title: Reports people act on: updates, insights and your capstone

say: Reports people act on: weekly updates, insights, and your capstone.
This is the video for module 4 of Reporting and Performance Tracking.

For example, Ruth manages sales for a drinks distributor in Enugu. Every Friday by 5 pm she sends her manager a WhatsApp update. First, the headline: sales of 412,000 naira against a target of 400,000. That is 103%.

panel.heading: The weekly update in five parts

say: Then what went well: a new school customer ordered 20 cartons.

panel.heading: The weekly update in five parts

say: Then the problem, stated plainly: the van broke down, and two customers complained about lateness.

panel.heading: The weekly update in five parts

say: Next week's actions: chase the 4 unpaid invoices by Tuesday, and call the two unhappy customers.

panel.heading: The weekly update in five parts

say: And help needed: approval for a van repair, with the 85,000 naira quote attached.
In under 80 words, her manager knows the result, the risk, the plan and his decision.

say: A monthly report starts with a short summary: the overall result, the biggest win, the biggest concern and your main recommendation.

panel.heading: A standard monthly report
items: KPI table: target and last month

say: Then a KPI table. Compare each KPI with the target and with last month. Below target but improving is a very different story from below target and falling.

panel.heading: A standard monthly report
items: KPI table: target and last month

say: Add the one or two charts that matter most.

panel.heading: A standard monthly report
items: KPI table: target and last month

say: Then explain what the numbers mean, and what should be done.

panel.heading: A standard monthly report
items: KPI table: target and last month

say: Finish with risks, and an appendix for definitions and corrections.

panel.heading: A standard monthly report
items: KPI table: target and last month

say: Many readers see only the summary and the KPI table, so make those clear. And send it on time, even with one figure marked to be confirmed.

panel.rule: Write the summary last, even though it comes first.

say: Numbers alone rarely change anything. Insights come from comparing. For example, Bisi splits her weekly sales of 70,000 naira by day. Saturday alone brings 28,000, which is 40%, more than Monday to Thursday combined.

cards.d: Saturday brings 28,000 of 70,000 naira: 40% of the week, more than Monday to Thursday.
Customers order for weekend gatherings. Her order-by-Thursday posts work well.
Add a Friday evening delivery slot for 4 weeks from 3 April, and track Friday sales.

say: So what? Her customers order for weekend gatherings, and her order by Thursday posts work.

cards.d: Saturday brings 28,000 of 70,000 naira: 40% of the week, more than Monday to Thursday.
Customers order for weekend gatherings. Her order-by-Thursday posts work well.
Add a Friday evening delivery slot for 4 weeks from 3 April, and track Friday sales.

say: Now what? Add a Friday evening delivery slot for 4 weeks, starting 3 April, and track whether Friday sales grow without reducing Saturday.
A strong recommendation has a specific action, an owner, a date, the KPI it should move, and any cost.

say: A funder wants to see that their money achieved what was agreed. Report against their exact indicators, with evidence, and show spending against budget.
Halima's budget is 1,500,000 naira. She has spent 1,200,000. That is 80% of the budget, at about 83% of the project time. Spending is slightly behind, because two sessions were cancelled.
The remaining 300,000 naira will fund the final and catch-up sessions.
And a money rule: many grant agreements need written approval before you move money from one budget line to another. Ask your funder before spending an underspend on something new.
Your capstone tracks a real metric for 2 to 3 weeks. For example, Grace runs a hair salon in Port Harcourt and wants to fill quiet weekday slots. Her baseline is 12 weekday bookings a week.

panel.heading: Grace's capstone in outline
items: Target: 15, a 25% rise, by end of week 3
Action: student discount on Tuesday and Wednesday
Insight: 4 students also bought a product

say: Her SMART target is 15 a week by the end of week 3. 12 times 1.25 is 15.

panel.heading: Grace's capstone in outline
items: Target: 15, a 25% rise, by end of week 3
Action: student discount on Tuesday and Wednesday
Insight: 4 students also bought a product

say: Her action is a Tuesday and Wednesday discount for students.

panel.heading: Grace's capstone in outline
items: Target: 15, a 25% rise, by end of week 3
Action: student discount on Tuesday and Wednesday
Insight: 4 students also bought a product

say: She gets 13, then 15, then 17 bookings. An average of 15, which is 100% of target.

panel.heading: Grace's capstone in outline
items: Target: 15, a 25% rise, by end of week 3
Action: student discount on Tuesday and Wednesday
Insight: 4 students also bought a product

say: Her insight: 9 of the 17 week 3 bookings were students, and 4 of them also bought a hair product. So she recommends keeping the discount another month, and tracking product sales to check it stays profitable.
Disappointing results are fine. The capstone is judged on honest tracking and reporting.

say: Before you submit, check every item. Goal, KPIs and target stated. Data checked. An honest chart. An insight that explains why. A recommendation with an owner and a date.
And remove names and phone numbers. Share it as a PDF, or as a link set to Restricted, with the reviewer as Viewer.

panel.heading: Capstone quality check
items: Names and numbers removed or coded

say: To remember. Keep weekly updates short and in five parts. Compare every KPI with the target and last month. Turn numbers into insights with What, So what, Now what.
Give funders their agreed indicators, evidence and budget use. And share reports safely.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Weekly: numbers, wins, problems, actions, help
Compare with target and with last month
Share safely: PDF or Restricted link

say: Now practise. Write a weekly update in under 120 words, and set up your monthly report template. Write three What, So what, Now what rows from your own dashboard. Then start your capstone, with your baseline and SMART target at the top of your sheet.
